item.title: MCU Breakout Star, 36, Hailed Christopher Nolan’s $758 Million Oscar-Winner as One of This Century’s Best Films
item.dc:creator: Adam Blevins
item.description: Christopher Nolan's $758 million Oscar-winner is hailed as one of this century's best by MCU breakout star.
item.content:encoded: Plenty of stars over the years have benefited from starring in Marvel movies that went on to become huge hits, but perhaps none more than Simu Liu. Relatively unheard of before starring in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, Liu has gone on to lead other hits like Barbie (Margot Robbie), Atlas (Sterling K. Brown), and Last Breath (Woody Harrelson). The New York Times recently released a list of the 100 best films of the 21st century, which included ballots from major Hollywood stars, writers, and directors. Liu was among those to earn a ballet, and he voted Interstellar as one of the best movies of the 21st century — the film finished in spot #89 on the list. Liu also voted for Inside Out, Get Out, La La Land, Tropic Thunder, and more in his list of 10.

item.title: John Cena and Idris Elba’s High-Octane Comedy Divides Critics on Rotten Tomatoes
item.dc:creator: Rahul Malhotra
item.description: Idris Elba and John Cena's new buddy comedy has gone rogue with critics as they split the score down the middle.
item.content:encoded: The last few years have seen an uptick in the production of a very particular kind of streaming movie; these films are typically flat to look at, often revolve around spies and global intrigue, and are sometimes designed to start franchises. Apple made Ghosted, starring Ana de Armas and Chris Evans; Netflix produced Heart of Stone, headlined by Gal Gadot; and now, Prime Video has delivered Heads of State, an action comedy with an A-list cast and an exciting filmmaker at the helm. However, the movie has earned mediocre reviews, and is currently sitting at a rather unimpressive Rotten Tomatoes score just ahead of its release on July 2.

item.title: ‘The Chosen’ Delivers Its Most Haunting Scene Yet: “It’s Not Something I Would Ever Want To Shoot Again"
item.dc:creator: Britta DeVore
item.description: The Chosen Season 6 delivers one of its most haunting scenes, and its star says he wouldn't want to shoot it again.
item.content:encoded: For the most part, Prime Video’s The Chosen has kept it light and bright. The first five seasons of the Biblical production followed the life of Jesus (Jonathan Roumie) as he began his religious outreach, drawing in his followers one by one. Darker scenes like demonic possessions have been scattered throughout the episodes, but, for the most part, it’s largely been a series that reflects the positive side of humanity. However, by the end of the most recent season, that theme flipped on its head with the arrest of Jesus at the hands of the Romans. Those familiar with the Bible know what happens next — Jesus is taken into custody, tried, and crucified.

item.title: ‘Superman’ Star, 34, Reveals the Secret Behind Lois Lane’s "Punk Rock" Backstory [Exclusive]
item.dc:creator: Chris McPherson
Perri Nemiroff
item.description: Superman's Rachel Brosnahan reveals new details about the backstory she and James Gunn have cooked up for Lois Lane. Read on for more.
item.content:encoded: There’s more to Lois Lane than meets the eye — and Superman star Rachel Brosnahan is happy to finally talk about it. In a fun sit-down alongside co-star David Corenswet, with Collider’s Perri Nemiroff, the 34-year-old actress opened up about how she and director James Gunn shaped the off-screen past of the iconic reporter — and how that past subtly informs everything we’ll see on screen. While Superman may center around Clark Kent’s heroic journey, it’s Lois who arrives with a little more emotional mileage. And that’s no accident.

item.title: The Mitfords Look for a Reason to Smile in 'Outrageous' Episode 4 Sneak Peek Clip [Exclusive]
item.dc:creator: Jake Hodges
item.description: A sneak peek from Outrageous episode 4 sees The Mitfords discuss politics whilst a photographer tries to take a pleasant picture.
item.content:encoded: Still furious about My Lady Jane's cancellation or missing your fill of Bridgerton? Why aren't you watching Outrageous? Currently streaming on BritBox, the latest British historical drama to take on the notorious Mitford sisters and their many tales is already a huge success, having earned a remarkable 88% critics' score on review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes from 17 reviews. This is both 4% higher than Bridgerton's total critics' score and an impressive 14% higher than its audience rating. So far, three episodes of Outrageous have aired, and they have certainly lived up to their name, with Collider excitingly teaming up with BritBox to exclusively reveal this clip of the upcoming fourth episode.

item.title: 'Yellowstone' Star, 41, Admits to One of the Hardest Parts of Being in Taylor Sheridan's Epic Series
item.dc:creator: Chris McPherson
item.description: Yellowstone star admits to one of the hardest parts of being in Taylor Sheridan's epic series.
item.content:encoded: Luke Grimes didn’t plan on returning to the Yellowstone universe—at least, not without a good reason. The 41-year-old actor, best known for playing Kayce Dutton across five seasons of Taylor Sheridan’s modern Western epic, says he was fully prepared to hang up his cowboy hat after the series ended last fall. But as he tells People, saying goodbye to Yellowstone wasn’t as easy as he expected.

item.title: 'Bosch' Spin-Off Creator Clarifies Titus Welliver's Role After 'Legacy' Cancellation
item.dc:creator: Chris McPherson
item.description: Bosch spin-off creator Michael Connelly clarifies Titus Welliver's role in Ballard after Legacy's cancellation.
item.content:encoded: Harry Bosch may have stepped out of Bosch: Legacy, but he’s far from retired. In fact, the iconic detective—played by Titus Welliver, 63—is set to play a major role in the upcoming Ballard series, according to Bosch creator and bestselling author Michael Connelly. The new show, led by Maggie Q as LAPD Detective Renée Ballard, will continue the gritty crime saga when it premieres on Prime Video, and Bosch’s involvement will be far more than a nostalgic walk-on.

item.title: Tom Cruise Takes Down His Steven Spielberg Sci-Fi Epic At the International Box Office With ‘Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning’
item.dc:creator: Rahul Malhotra
item.description: Tom Cruise takes down his own alien invasion movie with Mission: Impossible — The Final Reckoning at the international box office.
item.content:encoded: Over a month into its theatrical release, director Christopher McQuarrie's Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning is winding down at the box office. The movie didn't turn out to be the breakout hit that it was expected to, and will likely conclude its run with just over $600 million worldwide. While it's poised to overtake its direct predecessor, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning, in a day or two, its massive reported budget still doesn't make it a bona fide hit. That being said, The Final Reckoning has now overtaken one of star Tom Cruise's past hits, the acclaimed War of the Worlds.

item.title: It Looks Like the ‘Fast and Furious’ Franchise Has Lost Its Way
item.dc:creator: Collier Jennings
item.description: Vin Diesel's announcements for Fast X: Part 2 might have had fans scratching their heads, and wondering if the franchise will crash and burn.
item.content:encoded: Fans of the Fast & Furious films were hit with a bombshell wave of announcements this weekend, as longtime star & producer Vin Dieseltook the stage at FuelFest to update fans on the status of Fast & Furious 11. Chief among those announcements, which included a release date of April 2027, was that after years of delivering progressively intense stunts, the franchise would conclude with a story that took it back to its street racing roots. But the biggest bombshell was that Brian O'Connor—played by the late Paul Walker—would be making a return. While Diesel said that those were the three conditions that he and Universal agreed to, these feel less like a way to get the Fast & Furious films "back to basics" and more like the franchise has finally flown off the rails.

item.title: 'How to Train Your Dragon' Overtakes the Domestic Box Office of One of the Best War Movies Ever
item.dc:creator: Rahul Malhotra
item.description: How to Train Your Dragon overtakes the domestic box office of one of the best war movies ever.
item.content:encoded: Having played in theaters worldwide for less than a month, Universal's How to Train Your Dragon remake is all set to overtake the original animated film, which debuted 15 years ago. The live-action remake passed the $450 million mark at the worldwide box office this past weekend, while also hitting the $200 million milestone domestically. This puts it ahead of one of the highest-grossing World War II movies ever made. How to Train Your Dragon is also overtaking the recent Marvel Cinematic Universe underperformer Captain America: Brave New World on the domestic charts, as it aims to conclude its run as one of the 200 highest-grossing movies ever made.
